chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all from Safwan, who said: Abu Uyayna narrated to us from Zurara.

He said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I performed Zihar with a mother of a child of mine, then I had intercourse with her, then I expiated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is what the Faqih (jurist) does; when he has intercourse, he expiates.'

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (wife who bore his child)
key_terms.ظَاهَرْتُ: I performed Zihar (declaring wife like mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Zihar when a man has intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the juristic principle that the act of sexual intercourse itself serves as the expiation (Kaffarah) for Zihar, a ruling derived directly from the Quranic verse 'Then let him free a slave before they touch each other' (58:3). The Imam’s comparison to a 'Faqih' suggests that this immediate expiation is the standard legal practice for scholars, emphasizing that the physical act fulfills the condition of 'touching' mentioned in the revelation, thereby resolving the marital prohibition without requiring a separate divorce proceeding.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, altogether, from Safwan, narrated from Abu Uyayna, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘I did Zahaar from a mother of a child of mine, then I copulated upon her, then I expiated’. So heasws said: ‘This is how the understanding man (Faqih) does, when an expiation occurs (meaning he always pays the expiation if he does Zahaar)’.
en.sarwar: 29. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh all from Safwan who has said that abu ‘Uyaynah narrated from Zurarah

who has said the following: “I once said to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I have expressed the statement of al-Zihar about the mother of my children, then went to bed with her, then paid the expiation. He (the Imam) said, ‘This is how a faqih (scholar of law) man does; when he goes to bed he pays expiation.’”
